articleTitle: Tree-Based Sequential Sampling for Efficient Designs in Package Electrical Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 28th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: The use of surrogate models (SMs) has become popular in electromagnetic (EM) design and optimization. Traditional SMs, while beneficial, are often hindered by the inherent complexity and nonlinearity of EM systems, leading to challenges in data representation and design space exploration. Addressing these challenges, we introduce a novel tree-based learning strategy for sampling within high-dimensional EM design spaces. Our method emphasizes the localized exploration to accurately capture the unique output behaviors at various frequencies in multi-frequency EM simulations. The proposed method focuses on refining the sampling process instead of optimizing an objective function. The resulting strategy is a robust, nonparametric learning approach that facilitates the sequential selection of design configurations, promoting uniform accuracy in the sampled data. It also enhances the interpretability in high-dimensional spaces and provides a variable importance measure for output profile discrimination. Our empirical results show that this strategy improves the learning trajectory of SMs against random sampling from a Latin hypercube design.

articleTitle: A Dual-Polarized Quad-Ridged Waveguide Antenna for OTA Near-Field ATE Socket in 5G-FR2 Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 28th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel dual-polarized antenna design for over the air (OTA) testing of 5G antenna in package (AiP) modules in high volume manufacturing (HVM) using commercial automated test equipment (ATE). The requirements for such measurement antenna are first the wide bandwidth to cover all the frequency bands of the 5G-FR2 standard (24 to 53 GHz). Second, the antenna requires a very low profile to fit in the change kit of a commercial automated packaged integrated circuit handler for AiP devices production testing. In this paper the measurement antenna design is described. Its wideband performance has been verified with measurements of a manufactured prototype. Also, the developed antenna integration on a device under test (DUT) socket for near-field OTA HVM testing is presented.

articleTitle: Modeling and Analysis of Digital-to-Analog Converter Non-Idealities in Microwave Kinetic Inductance Detectors Readout
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 28th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: The Microwave Kinetic Inductance Detector (MKID) is a millimeter-wave-length light detector made with a radiofrequency superconductor resonator that exhibits the characteristic of high resonance quality factor (Q), enabling the multiplexing of hundreds of MKIDs on a single signal transmission line. In this study, we investigate the Digital-to-Analog Converter (DAC) of the current readout solution. Specifically, we developed a functional model of the DAC, including its slew rate and saturation limitations, and demonstrated its validity by comparing it with measurement results. This model allows to analyze the influence of the DAC's limitations across the entire frequency spectrum, and to examine its impact on the maximum frequency multiplexing factor. We demonstrate that the non-idealities of the DAC limit the maximum frequency multiplexing factor, which depends on the number of sinusoids, their amplitude, and phase.

articleTitle: Modeling of IC Buffers from Channel Responses Via Machine Learning Kernel Regression
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 28th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of a fully behavioral approach for the generation of accurate models of digital IC buffers based on conventional kernel regressions. The proposed approach does not assume a specific model structure like the classical two-piece model representation which has been massively used in literature, offering a promising and viable alternative to facilitate the modeling of nonlinear electrical devices. The collected results represent a first proof-of-concept, aimed at demonstrating the strengths of the proposed alternative modeling approach.

articleTitle: Methodology for Optimizing Ethernet Links at 10 and 25 Gbps for Critical Systems in the Aerospace Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 28th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: The design flow of a board with high-speed links can be time-consuming and requires a meticulous study of all parameters that may affect signal quality. The path of a high-speed signal passes through various structures that can create impedance discontinuities, such as BGA (Ball Grid Array), vias, AC coupling capacitors, or connectors. Poorly matched impedance can lead to unwanted signal reflections, energy losses, and electromagnetic interference. Each of these elements must be carefully analyzed to minimize the overall impact of each transition. This optimization work must take into account manufacturing constraints, frequency-dependent properties of materials, cost, as well as the reality of routing density that limits available space. An efficient methodology and design rules are developed to prepare for future designs and push the technological boundaries of aerospace products.

articleTitle: Impact of Port Type in S-Parameter Extraction of Package and PCB High-Speed Interconnections
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 28th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: Modern digital devices are characterized by an increasing density of high-speed signal interfaces running at growing frequencies. In this context, a reliable characterization of the signal interconnections is fundamental and requires a very accurate modeling approach, relying on 3D electromagnetic simulation tools. For BGA (Ball Grid Array) packages, due to the high routing density and the small dimensions, crosstalk is becoming a very critical quantity to be verified through s-parameters extraction and compared with application targets. S-parameters require the definition of ports at the terminals of the extracted lines, and this can be done with different methods. Focus of this paper is a comparison between circuit ports and coaxial ports, with the purpose of understanding how the port type can influence the simulation results. The fact that a specific port type requires the addition of dedicated geometry elements to make it work (i.e. an additional reference plane) is a key aspect in this study, since it changes the boundary conditions versus the original design. After presenting a series of comparative tests, the port type impact is characterized, and the optimal setup is identified considering the test case of a high-speed signal bus on a BGA package. As an extension, similar tests are performed on a PCB, confirming the same findings besides some intrinsic differences.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Effects of Power Partitioning in LPDDR4x Package for Enhanced EMC Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 28th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: Considering the characteristics of data sensing, noise blocking, and Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) within DRAM, we investigated the method of partitioning power islands in package PCB, through experiments and simulations. When the power of the core die (VDD2A_PKG) and the power of the interface circuit (VDD2B_PKG) were merged, there was little difference in terms of I/O signal transfer characteristics. However, from the EMI perspective, there was an improvement of about 10dB compared to the case with split powers. The simulation results indicate that integrating the core power and IO interface power within the LPDDR4x's PKG PCB is beneficial for reducing EMI. These findings are consistent with experimental results.

articleTitle: Prediction of Power Supply Induced Jitter via Deep Belief and Knowledge-Based Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 28th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: In this paper, a hybrid neural network approach using deep belief and knowledge-based neural networks is developed to handle multiple noise sources including supply noise, ground bounce noise and input data noise while evaluating power supply induced jitter (PSIJ). The proposed hybrid approach provides reasonable accuracy for jitter response using training data from semi-analytical models as well as a circuit simulator. The proposed model can handle different types of inputs without needing to update the network's parameters for each case while ensuring faster convergence.

articleTitle: Analyzing Performance of Nonlinear High-Speed Links Based on Least Square Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 28th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: This paper proposes a method to analyze the performance of nonlinear high-speed links based on the least square method. In this method, two matrices constructed from the input bits and output waveforms are used as inputs to the least square method. By fitting these matrices, a matrix that represents the nonlinear characteristics of the link is obtained, and this matrix is then used to calculate the statistical eye diagram. Comparing the proposed method with transient simulation, single-edge response method and double-edge response method demonstrates that the proposed method possesses not only the efficiency of the single-edge response method but also the accuracy of the double-edge response method.

articleTitle: Segmented Cavity Design for Suppression of Cavity-to-Via Coupling in High-Speed Transmission Lines of Multi-Layer Printed Circuit Boards
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 28th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: This paper proposes a segmented cavity structure designed to enable high-speed signal transmission in high-aspect-ratio multi-layer printed circuit boards (MLPCBs). The proposed structure is designed to suppress group cavity resonance, a phenomenon that couples with signal vias as they transition between layers and causes broadband signal degradation in high-speed transmission lines. The proposed design structures were validated through 3-dimensional electromagnetic field simulation, demonstrating improved signal integrity performance.

articleTitle: Signal and Power Integrity Co-Simulation of Chiplet-to-Chiplet Channel Based on Latency Insertion Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 28th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: This paper introduces a transient simulation approach for conducting signal and power integrity analysis in chiplet systems based on Latency Insertion Method (LIM). LIM is utilized to simulate the system including power distribution network (PDN), the drivers in the chips, and the interconnection between chiplets. The PDN and chip drivers are represented through equivalent circuit models. And the channels are treated as blackbox networks characterized by scattering parameters, and are incorporated to LIM through macromodeling. The proposed method is capable of providing transient analysis results, including on-chip voltage fluctuations induced by the PDN and signal propagation through the inter-chiplet channels. It can demonstrate how imperfections in the PDN can impact signal integrity, offering valuable insights for optimizing system in package (SiP) design.

articleTitle: Leveraging SIMPLIS to Better Predict Server Platform Power Delivery Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 28th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: Voltage regulator (VR) and power delivery network (PDN) models are critical to the design of server platforms. Inaccurate models can result in over-design, leading to increased costs or an under-design, which can lead to performance deterioration. Tools, such as HSPICE and SIMPLIS, are used to predict the performance of server platform power delivery systems. These tools have different strengths and weaknesses, e.g., HSPICE provides more reliable results in the first voltage droop timing of the waveforms but does not accurately model the behavior of more complex nonlinear VR controllers, and SIMPLIS provides better modeling of the VR response and more reliable results in the third voltage droop timing but can have longer simulation times depending on the complexity of the circuit. A methodology whereby VR models and lab results can be leveraged to improve the overall system level models in both SIMPLIS and HSPICE, through a series of measurement-simulation correlation processes is presented in this paper. Different case studies, including server processor core maximum current (Imax) prediction and Vmin predictability, using this methodology and resulting models, are also presented.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Near-Field Scanning with a Spatially Sparse Sampling Strategy Utilizing Kriging-DMD
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 28th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: This paper proposes a hybrid method for time-resolved electromagnetic near-field scanning, merging model-based (Gaussian processes regression model, a.k.a. Kriging method) and data-driven (dynamic mode decomposition) techniques. Specifically, Latin hypercube sampling enables spatially sparse measurements, followed by dynamic mode decomposition to analyze resulting sparse spatial-temporal data, extracting frequency information and sparse dynamic modes. The Kriging method is then employed for full-state reconstruction. The proposed approach is evaluated using crossed dipole antennas. Results indicate that, even with a spatial subsampling factor of 130, achieving a fully reconstructed field distribution suitable for engineering applications with frequency information extraction is feasible. This hybrid framework presents a promising avenue to enhance efficiency in electromagnetic near-field measurements, potentially finding applications across diverse electromagnetic measurement scenarios.

articleTitle: On the Performance Analysis of Automatic Gain Control Module in Quantized OFDM 5G Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 28th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: This work analyzes the impact of a digital automatic gain control (AGC) module within quantized orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) systems for fifth-generation (5G) networks due to the necessity of decreasing the effective number of bits (ENOBs) in analog-to-digital converters (ADCs). Diverse data sources, including simulation and laboratory data, are employed in the AGC design process. The results demonstrate the AGC's adaptability across nine different ENOB configurations. Furthermore, a hardware implementation of the AGC is executed, revealing a significantly low resource usage and emphasizing its practicality for real-world applications.

articleTitle: Complete System Analysis of High Speed Serial Interfaces of Data Rate up to 20 Gbps with IBIS-AMI Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 28th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: As handheld electronic equipment becomes more compact, it also demands higher performance. To achieve the overall best performance of the system, Printed Circuit Boards (PCB) are embedding different best-suited blocks from different IP vendors. This integration often results in the use of different transmitters and receivers from different-different IP vendors within the same module. Consequently, there is a growing need for a universally accepted Computer-Aided Design (CAD) model that can support high-speed serial interfaces. This paper describes a model known as I/O Buffer Information Specifications-Algorithmic Modeling Interface (IBIS-AMI), including its generation and verification steps for a reference design and its uses in complete system analysis. The reference design used in this study is a PHY transmitter with an operating data rate of up to 20Gbps with different signal processing features like multi-level pre-cursor, post-cursor de-emphasis, multiple-level differential swing, and choices of output differential impedances. To evaluate the complete system, the IBIS-AMI model of the PHY transmitter has been used and the effects of various transmitter parameters (swing, pre-cursor, and post-cursor de-emphasis) on the overall system performance has been analyzed. This paper also discusses the results to better understand how the system behaves at various electrical settings.

articleTitle: Time Domain Assessment of Minimum FEXT by Tabbed Line Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 28th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: Tabbed lines have been demonstrated to be effective for the reduction of Far-End Crosstalk (FEXT) in coupled lines and data bus of microstrip type. A minimum FEXT can be identified by carefully designing the tab geometry, the tab-to-tab distance, and the percentage of the tabbed portion of the microstrip with respect to the entire length. This paper evaluates the time domain performances of tabbed lines to verify their performances in terms of FEXT minimization. The induced FEXT pulse and the eye diagram metrics are used to demonstrate the tabs impact to reach a minimum FEXT. The dB level of the FEXT S-parameter that is necessary to reach to minimize the eye closure is derived while analyzing both DDR4 signals running at 3.2 Gbps and DDR5 signals running at 4.8 Gbps.

articleTitle: Uncertainty Quantification of the Insertion Loss of an Automotive PCB Stripline
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 28th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: In this combination of measurement and modeling, the relative effect of process variations present in the cross-section dimensions and material properties of two automotive printed circuit boards (PCBs), with 10-inch striplines is studied. Specifically, the insertion loss (IL) uncertainty up to 20 GHz. The PCBs were horizontally cut into fifteen cross-section samples each. Normal distributions were obtained after measurements of their physical dimensions and for the PCB dielectric properties, a uniform distribution was selected. The measured distributions in combination with assumed stochastic variations for the dielectric properties of the striplines were used to simulate a 2D cross-section via an electromagnetic (EM) 2D-Method of Moments (MoM) solver. The sensitivities due to the input variables were obtained through a second order polynomial chaos expansion (PCE) in two different analysis. The first case focused on the measured physical dimensions variability and showed that the conductor roughness had the biggest effect on the IL uncertainty. The second case analyzed the combination between measured data and the assumed stochastic variation of the dielectric properties; and showed a bigger dependence of the IL uncertainty due to the dielectric properties than the physical dimensions.

articleTitle: Validation of Switching Voltage Regulator Noise Mitigation to Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 28th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: Switching voltage regulator noise has been a critical negative impact to signal integrity failure, and a well-considered board design is essential in advance. In this work, we analyze three common coupling paths from a VRM (voltage regulator module) to signals: broadside, orthogonal, and vertical coupling. Then we investigate the dominance of each coupling mechanism and validate the switching noise mitigation in a real-world server system. Based on the findings, the noise reduction techniques, extending the distance and applying the back drilling, have been demonstrated in both simulation and measurement methods.

articleTitle: PCB Based Power Delivery Network Analysis Using Transfer Learning and Artificial Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 28th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: In this paper, the applicability of transfer learning (TL) combined with artificial neural networks (ANNs) for power integrity analysis of printed circuit boards (PCBs) is investigated. Reusing already existing data samples from a database enables to reduce the amount of data samples required for a new problem setting. Here, more than 30 000 electromagnetic numerical simulations are evaluated of different PCB shapes, geometries, and used materials. The format and processing of the data is adapted at hand, e.g. the plane capacitance is used as one additional input feature. If less than 50 training samples are available the error is reduced by a factor 2 using TL.

articleTitle: High Sensitivity Sensors Based on Slit Plasmonic Gold Nanoantennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 28th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: In this research work, a novel model is used to analyse the propagation of Surface Plasmon Polaritons and the Extraordinary Optical Transmission effect. The model is based on generalised Fresnel Coefficients and wave-particle dualism. An oriented-object program is developed in Python to implement the model. This novel model brings geometrical intuition to complex electromagnetic problems and taking advantage of that, two kinds of sensors are designed at nano-scale and femtoseconds orders. Furthermore, by combining the working principles of both sensors, it is analysed if more sensitive ones may be designed. A gold nanoantenna is analysed as a tilt angle sensor in a 1.33–1.35 analyte, being concluded that angles are distinguished by analysing the optical intensity on the detected, which has variations between 2–10%. On the other hand, the gold nanoantenna is also able to monitor refractive index variations between 1.33 and 1.35. Sensitivities between 50–100%/RIU are obtained and it is concluded that by tilting the emission angle the sensitivity to the refractive index variation may be tuned.

articleTitle: Fast Error-Bounded MOR-Based Approximation of Heat Conduction Problems in Electronics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 28th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: The Moment Matching Method, optimized with a proper choice of matching points, is shown to allow the fast computation of an error-bound approximation to the solution of transient heat conduction problems in practical electronics applications, both in the time and frequency domain.

articleTitle: Mean-Free-Path-Based Evaluation of Size Effect and Anomalous Skin Effect in On-Chip Interconnects Under Cryogenic Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 28th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: This paper investigates the impact of size effect and anomalous skin effect in on-chip interconnects under cryogenic environment. Cryo-CMOS technology is required for quantum computers. At cryogenic temperature, the electron-mean-free-path becomes longer and surface scattering becomes dominant factor to determine the resistivity. Also, anomalous skin effect affects the frequency characteristics. I investigate the impact of the size effect and the anomalous skin effect by evaluating the electron-mean-free-path considering surface scattering. Numerical evaluation reveals that size-dependency of the resistivity and the anomalous skin effect have to be taken into consideration.

articleTitle: Electro-Thermal Response of Industrial-Grade Graphene for Electronic Packages Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 28th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: This paper deals with the electro-thermal characterization of strips of industrial-grade graphene in view of their use as advanced novel materials for electronic packages, for instance, as Thermal Interface Materials. The analyzed material is a low-cost version of graphene, realized by combining commercial graphene nanoplatelets, and thus suitable for mass production. The electrical resistivity is shown to be almost stable with temperature, with a slightly negative derivative. The thermal conductivity is found to exhibit very good values, lower than that of pure graphene, but still interesting for practical cases. Thermal time constants are estimated in the range of seconds, providing faster thermal transients compared to classical materials.

articleTitle: On the Performance Analysis of DL-Based Data Detection Algorithms in $M$-QAM Satellite Links
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 28th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: This work presents an analysis of deep learning (DL)-based data detection algorithms in the context of satellite communications, specifically considering challenging atmospheric environments (CAE). Since the satellite-to-earth communication systems migration to high-frequency bands, the influence of rain, fog, clouds, and vapors becomes more pronounced, imposing challenges for channel estimation. Thus, the adoption of DL-based data detection algorithms offers an alternative approach to improve the end-to-end performance. In our work, the performance of these algorithms is evaluated using the bit error rate (BER) metric in CAEs, considering Ku and K frequency bands. To the best of the author's knowledge, this study is the first to adopt and investigate the impact of atmospheric effects on DL-based data detection.

articleTitle: Dimensional Reduction by Auto-Encoders in Machine Learning Based Power Integrity Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 28th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: This study<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>This work is funded by the German federal ministry for economic affairs and climate action of the Federal Republic of Germany under the funding code 19A21006R delves into the application of auto-encoders (AE) to reduce the large dimension of the parameter space for design problems of printed circuit boards (PCB). After dimensional reduction to an adequate sized latent space with controlled information loss, efficient machine learning (ML) methods, such as artificial neural networks (ANN), can support the analysis and the design of PCBs by operating on latent space data. As an example the combination of a trained encoder and a downstream ANN for predicting impedances between various ports of a complex PCB is studied. The decoder of the AE can subsequently be used to remap a latent space representation of PCB data back into the physical space. The efficiency of dimensional reduction due to an AE is compared to low dimensional representation of impedance responses via vector fitting. Finally, SHAP (Shapley Additive Explanations) values are employed to show the significance of individual design parameters on impedance responses. Frameworks linking dimensional reduction by AEs with ANN-based predictive models may provide deeper insights into the complex interactions within PCBs, enable precise predictions of their electrical properties, and, thus, support PCB design.

articleTitle: Analysis of Optimum Rotation Angle for Mitigating P/N Skew Based on Geometrical Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 28th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: In this paper, a geometrical method is proposed to analyze the effect of rotation angle to the P/N skew. The simplified grid model is used to represent the 3D weaved glass fiber structure and the volume ration of glass and resin is used to compute the equivalent dielectric constant. Based on that equivalent dielectric constant, a geometrical method is proposed to compute the distribution of P/N skew with the rotated angles and the relative locations of traces to the glass weave. The results have reasonable agreement with the simulated results by 3D electromagnetic simulators. The optimal rotated angle for mitigating the P/N skew is analyzed which shows that the best rotation angel depends on the trace and the glass wave parameters.

articleTitle: Efficient Investigation of Coupled Lines in Quasi Periodical High-Density Signal Routings for HPC Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 28th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: In this paper, a method for efficient and rigorous analysis of cross coupling in a very dense periodical arrangement of signal lines in re-distribution layers of silicon-based interposers is presented. The proposed method reduces the calculation in a complex multi-conductor and multilayer structure to a very small number of time-consuming field calculations. Some examples related to a polymer-based silicon interposer showing the nature of the aggressor's field propagation through neighboring traces depending on the position of the aggressor and victim conductors are presented. Very good correlation between the proposed method and commercial fields solvers such as CST are obtained.

articleTitle: Models and Methods for the Analysis of PCB Crosstalk in Switch-Mode Power Supplies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 28th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: This paper deals with the problem of evaluating the electromagnetic coupling between the traces of printed circuit boards. Specifically, the paper insights into models and methods applicable to extract the parasitic mutual capacitance, assuming the typical operating conditions of hard-switching switch-mode power supplies. The case study analyzed herein refers to the unwanted coupling between traces related to power and control sub-circuits. Several approaches are compared, and implemented in commercial simulation tools, spanning a variety of models, from static 2D ones to full-wave 3D ones. Some simple criteria are assessed to guide the correct use of such tools, depending on the physical and geometrical parameters of the problem.

articleTitle: Evaluating Deep Reinforcement Learning for Macromodel Synthesis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 28th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to apply reinforcement learning (RL) to the design of equivalent circuits for modeling passive electronic components. These components are usually characterized by S-parameter measurements in the frequency domain. However, time-domain simulations and other applications require equivalent circuit models. Baseline methods for generating these models have drawbacks, such as requiring prior physical knowledge of the components, generating large models with unnecessary lumped elements, or violating passivity rules. We present an RL-based approach to this problem by developing an RL environment in which the design of an equivalent circuit can be considered as a Markov Decision Process (MDP). In this way, we enable an RL agent to interact with the MDP in a stepwise manner with the goal of generating a best-fitting equivalent circuit for a component. A spice-assisted approach within the RL environment ensures the passivity of the equivalent circuit. With the presented experiment, we provide a first proof of concept for this approach and discuss future possibilities and challenges of this method.

articleTitle: Fast Prediction of Worst-Case Voltage Droops in Power Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 28th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: Building on well-known system theoretical results, simple numerical tools are introduced for the evaluation of the worst-case voltage droops in Power Distribution Networks (PDN), in various Power Integrity verification scenarios. Given a PDN model and suitable bounds on load current values and slew rates, the proposed approach provides an explicit bound of the worst-case voltage droop, as well as the particular input current waveforms that produce it. Validations are provided based on two realistic PDN models.

articleTitle: Differential Interconnects with Integrated Equalization and Common-Mode Filtering for Broadband Signal Integrity Enhancement in High-Speed PAM-4 Signaling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 28th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: In high-speed differential interconnects on printed circuit boards, signal integrity (SI) issues arise when neglecting the inherent low-pass characteristic and ubiquitous presence of common-mode noise. This work proposes a novel open-circuited stub equalizer with integrated common-mode filter in order to compensate for the low-pass characteristic while simultaneously suppressing the transmission of unwanted common-mode noise to the receiver. A theoretical analysis of the open-circuited stub equalizer is conducted, and suitable approximations are derived to facilitate equalizer synthesis. Experimental validation is provided by a test structure consisting of a 20 cm microstrip serpentine delay line for which a 4 GHz equalizer is designed. Frequency-domain measurements show a 1-dB bandwidth up to 3.97 GHz with a passband ripple of 0.38 dB for the differential mode and a significant reduction in transmission for the common mode. The resulting SI enhancement increases the possible data rate from 6 Gbps to 20 Gbps using a PAM-4 (pulse amplitude modulation 4-level) modulation scheme.

articleTitle: Automatic PCB Material Characterization Using Design of Experiments and Mixed-Integer Sequential Quadratic Programming
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 28th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: The growing demand for higher data rate SerDes channel calls for better PCB channel modelling. Conductor surface roughness can no longer be ignored, and it must be accurately modelled. PCB material characterization is a reliable methodology to extract roughness parameters from the lab measurement. The characterization process calibrates a transmission line model against lab measurement in terms of insertion loss and phase. However, manual calibration is not an easy task to get excellent broadband fitting for both insertion loss and phase. This paper introduces an automatic calibration approach based on Design of Experiments (DoE) and Mixed-Integer Sequential Quadratic Programming (MISQP).

articleTitle: Application of Gaussian Process Regression for Data Efficient Prediction of PCB-Based Power Delivery Network Impedance Features
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 28th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: In this paper, a data efficient machine learning (ML)-based framework for the prediction of key-features of the power delivery network (PDN) impedance is proposed. Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) is implemented within transfer and active learning loops to explore the potential with regard to data efficiency and accuracy. For a 4 layered printed circuit board (PCB), a prediction accuracy with a normalized root mean squared error (RMSE) of 3 % is achieved for some features including the resonance frequency of the board. The use of transfer learning results in a higher data efficiency and faster convergence. It is shown that reusing data from closer problems reduces the amount of new samples that need to be generated. The higher data efficiency makes ML tools a more attractive approach to speed up PDN design by replacing the expensive electromagnetic (EM) simulations of PCBs.

articleTitle: Abnormal-State-Clustering for In-Vehicle Cable Communication Using Equalizer Parameters and Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 28th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: In this paper, an abnormal-state-clustering method for the in-vehicle communication is proposed. The proposed method uses a full set of an equalizer's tap coefficient parameters that can be obtained from serializer/deserializer devices. The difference in the tap coefficient parameters between the normal state and the abnormal state is calculated and used for a characteristic parameter of abnormal-state-clustering. We also utilize a machine learning approach to obtain high accuracy for abnormal-state-clustering from multidimensional parameters of the difference in the tap coefficient. We verified the effectiveness of our approach in a simulation. Classification accuracy high as 96.4% was achieved by using a decision tree with dimension reduction in the principal component analysis.

articleTitle: Advanced Package Decoupling Study for Power Integrity Optimization of High-End Digital Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 28th Workshop on Signal and Power Integrity (SPI)
abstract: In the context of power integrity optimization for high-end digital devices, integration of decoupling capacitors on BGA (Ball Grid Array) packages is becoming a critical aspect. With increasing requirements in terms of functions integration and power consumption, combined with lower noise margins, miniaturization and cost reduction, a deep analysis is needed to achieve the maximum improvement at all the levels of the system (package, die, application board). This paper describes a methodology to optimize package decoupling, starting from a large capacitors portfolio and progressively reducing the options while moving from the frequency-domain to the time-domain analysis. As second step, the use of alternative technologies to reduce the parasitic inductances and improve the decoupling effectiveness is explored. Part of the work is to identify the boundaries of package decoupling effectiveness, beyond which other portions of the system (die or board) must be involved in the optimization process.
